text:
jamie: Heads-up — planning a preemptible/spot chaos game day next Tue 9:00am PT. Goal: validate mixed-capacity pools, interruption handling, and failover to on-demand without user impact.

nico: SGTM. Scope: which regions / clusters?

jamie: Start with us-west1 and europe-west2 (highest usage). Staged approach: staging smoke first, then a prod canary where ~20% of worker capacity is shifted to spot-backed nodes. We'll force evictions and observe autoscaler + routing behavior.

maria: Prefer to run a full staging rehearsal? worried about connector sessions during live evictions.

jamie: Yes — staging dry run at 08:50, prod canary at 09:05. Rollback policy: automatic routing revert if error rate >5% sustained over 5m.

ben: Success criteria to capture up front: errors <5%, median latency p95 <200ms, no KV cache state lost >1 minute, no rollbacks. Also expect cost reduction in canary of ~18–25% vs baseline.

tony: What about streaming sessions / long LLM streams? Need draining for active connections and connector-side retries.

jamie: Draining plan: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` + our grace script that waits up to 90s for KV/session handoffs. We'll also run forced-eviction cases to ensure model-variant fallback works (routing to quantized or on-demand replicas).

nico: I'll author a chaos script that triggers node preemptions via cloud API (GCE preempt, AWS terminate). It will tag evicted nodes with `chaos=preempted` and emit a metric `chaos.preempt.events` to Datadog.

sre-bot: Reminder: if you participate, update oncall rota with /reserve-game-day 9-11am. Bot will post escalation channel.

maria: Do we have an existing runbook for mixed-capacity autoscaler? Adding link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/preemptible-mix — will add KMS/HSM checks for private deploys too.

jamie: I'll open a runbook PR and create a #gd-1710701234 channel for play-by-play. Test harness called `spot-failover-checker` will exercise fallback; example API call: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/test/failover -d '{"model":"gpt-large","type":"fallthrough"}'```

ben: Also we need to simulate cache-warming and subsequent misses — real cost comes from re-tokenization and missed KV prefixes after eviction.

nico: Agreed. We'll seed KV cache with synthetic prefix hits before eviction and set short TTLs so we can measure rehydration time and extra token cost.

jamie: Postmortem/reporting: EOD summary due. Must include metrics: error rate, latency p50/p95/p99, model fallback %, cache miss rate, and cost delta vs baseline. Assignments: jamie (lead), nico (chaos scripts + tags), ben (SLO monitoring & dashboards), maria (runbook & security signoff), tony (connectors).

oncall: I'm on for 9-11 and will execute rollback if the >5% threshold is hit.

maria: :thumbsup: Adding runbook checklist now. Note: europe has lower spot availability — Nico, can you cap europe canary to 10% and fallback to dedicated if preemptions exceed threshold?

nico: Will do. Setting europe canary to 10% and adding region-aware capacity fallback in the script.

jamie: Thanks all. Dry run 08:50, live canary 09:05. Play-by-play and artifacts will be posted in #gd-1710701234. Keep messages short during the exercise so the channel stays scannable.
